title: Use Desmos Lists and List Tools
description: Create named lists, transform every value with list arithmetic, combine lists with join, and calculate mean, median, and total efficiently in Desmos.

blocks.html:
Give it a try

Spend about a minute on this question. Keep what you tried, even if you got stuck. You can continue without submitting an answer.

shared_prompt.title: Two sensors’ measurements
shared_prompt.html:
Sensor A reported each measurement as twice its actual value plus 3. Sensor B reported actual values correctly.

Reported measurements
SensorValues
A47, 29, 63, 35, 51, 39, 55
B15, 27, 21, 19, 25, 17

What is the median of all 13 actual measurements?

blocks.html:
Correct a whole group at once

The opening question asks you to correct seven measurements, combine them with six others, and find the middle value. Repeating those calculations and sorting by hand is tedious.

A list lets one operation work on a whole group. We’ll start with four values, then return to the sensors.

shared_prompt.title: List A data
shared_prompt.html: List \(A\) holds the values \(2,3,4,5\) in that order.

blocks.html:
Store the values

Type \(A=[2,3,4,5]\). Square brackets hold the list; commas separate its values. The equals sign defines \(A\) as that whole list.

content.hint: Put the list name before the equals sign and place comma-separated values inside square brackets.
content.explanation: \(A=[2,3,4,5]\) defines A as a four-value list.

blocks.html:
Your turn

Enter \(A=[2,3,4,5]\). Read the four values in the output.

Change every value at once

Arithmetic on a list acts on every value in it. For example, B=A+2 creates a new list by adding 2 to every value of A.

The same idea works for subtraction, multiplication, division, and powers. Desmos applies the operation to the whole list.

content.prompt: For \(A=[2,3,4,5]\), enter \(B=A+2\). What does Desmos show for B?
content.hint: Read the result displayed for B on the second expression line.
content.explanation: Every element of A increased by 2, so \(B=[4,5,6,7]\).

content.prompt: With \(A=[2,3,4,5]\), what list does Desmos display for \(3A\)?
content.hint: Read the three-times-A row in the calculator.
content.explanation: Multiplying a list by 3 multiplies every element by 3.

blocks.html:
Try another operation

With \(A=[2,3,4,5]\), enter \(3A\) and \(A^2\). Notice that each result still has four values.

content.hint: Square each value separately: 2 squared, 3 squared, 4 squared, and 5 squared.
content.explanation: Exponentiation applies to each element, giving \([4,9,16,25]\).

blocks.html:
Add matching positions

For \(A=[1,2,3]\) and \(B=[10,20,30]\), \(A+B\) gives \([11,22,33]\). It adds first to first, second to second, and third to third.

To keep all six original values, you need a different command.

content.prompt: What output does Desmos display for A+B?
content.hint: Read the list on the A+B row and compare it with the options.
content.explanation: List arithmetic pairs elements by position, so \(A+B=[11,22,33]\).

blocks.html:
Keep both groups with join

join combines complete lists. Type \(C=\operatorname{join}(A,B)\) to get \([1,2,3,10,20,30]\). Each original value stays in the combined list.

Compare the outputs

Read \(A+B\) and \(\operatorname{join}(A,B)\) in the calculator. Which output keeps all six original values?

content.hint: Keep the first list in order, then place the second list after it.
content.explanation: join connects the lists end to end, producing \([2,4,6,8]\).

content.prompt: You need one list containing every value from lists P and Q. Which command should you use?
content.hint: Arithmetic combines corresponding values. One list placed after another requires the list-combining function.
content.explanation: \(\operatorname{join}(P,Q)\) preserves every value and combines the lists end to end.

blocks.html:
Ask for one summary number

  • mean gives the average: \(\operatorname{mean}(A)\).
  • median gives the middle of the sorted data: \(\operatorname{median}(A)\).
  • total gives the sum: \(\operatorname{total}(A)\).

Try the summary commands

Read the three results for \(A=[2,3,4,5]\). Change one value in \(A\) and see how the results update.

content.hint: Read the result displayed by mean(A) in the calculator.

content.prompt: Which command finds the middle value of list D?
content.hint: The function name is the same as the statistic being requested.
content.explanation: median(D) asks Desmos for the middle of the data. The command handles sorting and any calculation needed.

content.prompt: For \(A=[2,3,4,5]\), what does Desmos display for \(\operatorname{total}(A)\)?
content.hint: Read the result on the total(A) row.
content.explanation: Desmos displays \(14\). The total command adds the values in the stored list.

blocks.html:
Find a command when you need it

Open the Functions menu. Look under Statistics for mean, median, and total, and under List Operations for join. Use a familiar command directly when you remember it.

Store, Choose, Read

  1. Store each group in square brackets.
  2. Choose arithmetic to change values, join to combine groups, or a summary command.
  3. Read the resulting list or number.

You can combine commands, such as \(\operatorname{mean}(\operatorname{join}(A,B))\).

Return to the sensor measurements

Try the opening question again. Find the median of the actual measurements from both sensors.

content.prompt: What is the median of all 13 actual measurements?
content.hint: Store the two groups separately. Undo Sensor A’s added 3 and doubling before combining the actual values and finding the median.
content.solution:
Enter \(A=[47,29,63,35,51,39,55]\) and \(B=[15,27,21,19,25,17]\).
Enter \(C=(A-3)/2\) to correct every Sensor A measurement.
Enter \(\operatorname{median}(\operatorname{join}(C,B))\).
Desmos displays \(21\).
content.explanation: You found \(21\). List arithmetic corrected the seven values together; join and median handled the combined group.

content.prompt: No notes: what do square brackets, list arithmetic, join, and mean / median / total each do in Desmos?
choices: Square brackets create lists; join transforms elements; arithmetic combines lists; mean, median, and total summarize data
Parentheses create lists; arithmetic transforms elements; join summarizes data; mean, median, and total combine lists
Square brackets create lists; arithmetic transforms only the first element; join combines lists; total is the only summary function
Square brackets create lists; arithmetic transforms elements; join combines lists; mean, median, and total summarize data
content.explanation: You have it. Define lists with square brackets, reuse their names, transform elements with arithmetic, combine groups with join, and summarize with mean, median, or total.

blocks.html:
Try it on your own

Choose the approach for each question. Try these now or save them for homework.

content.prompt: Group P recorded \([6,8,10]\), and Group Q recorded \([12,14]\). Which Desmos expression finds the mean of all five values?
content.explanation: join(P,Q) creates the five-value combined list, and mean finds its average.

content.prompt: Let \(A=[1,3]\) and \(B=[5,7]\). What list does \(\operatorname{join}(A,B)+1\) produce?
content.explanation: join makes \([1,3,5,7]\), and adding 1 transforms every element into \([2,4,6,8]\).

content.prompt: The mean of the data set \(11, 14, 19, 22, 24\) is \(18\). A new data set is created by increasing each value by \(6\). What is the mean of the new data set?
content.explanation: Enter \(A=[11,14,19,22,24]\), then \(\operatorname{mean}(A+6)\). Desmos displays \(24\), the mean of the changed data set.

Store once, reuse the list

Choose the operation that matches what the question asks.
